sentence: J'espère pouvoir y aller avec toi aujourd'hui.
english: I wish I could go with you today.
note: espérer = hope; 'I wish I could' is counterfactual; should be 'I hope I can go'

sentence: Afin de mieux vous servir, votre appel peut être enregistré.
english: In order to serve you better, your call may be monitored.

sentence: Mon arbre a quelques fleurs mais aucun fruit.
english: My tree had a few blossoms but no fruit.
note: French present tense; English past tense

sentence: Je pense, que nous sommes encore en Pologne !
english: I think we are still in Poland!

sentence: Je suis jaloux parce que tu as un bon patron.
english: I'm jealous because you have a good boss.
note: target F:as is an inflected form not the lemma avoir; no content target for jaloux/patron

sentence: Je m'occuperai de tes affaires quand tu seras mort.
english: I'll look after your affairs when you are dead.
note: morbid and context-bound; not a natural first example

sentence: Ils arrivèrent à l'hôtel à quatre heures.
english: At four o'clock, they arrived at the hotel.
note: passé simple (literary); learners will not hear it in speech

sentence: L'air est rare au sommet d'une haute montagne.
english: The air is thin at the top of a high mountain.
note: 'l'air est rare' is stilted; natural form is 'raréfié' or 'il y a peu d'air'

sentence: Pour sauver son crédit, il faut cacher sa perte.
english: To save your credit, you must conceal your loss.

sentence: C'était une bonne idée que de créer Tatoeba.
english: Creating Tatoeba was a good idea.
note: context-bound: needs to know Tatoeba; stilted 'que de' construction

sentence: Sur son visage, je vis un joyeux sourire.
english: I saw a joyful smile on his face.

sentence: Il posa la clé sur le bureau, comme d'habitude.
english: He put the key on the desk as usual.

sentence: Après une courte paix, la guerre éclata à nouveau.
english: After a brief peace, war broke out again.

sentence: La douleur est toujours moins forte que la plainte.
english: The pain is always milder than the moan.
note: proverb-like and odd in both languages; no clear everyday use

sentence: Mon patron m'a loué pour mon sérieux travail.
english: My boss praised me for my hard work.
note: 'loué' is ambiguous with 'rented'; 'sérieux travail' unnatural; 'hard' loose for 'sérieux'

sentence: La science médicale est toujours en marche.
english: Medical science is always on the march.
